description: Defines how A.R.I.A. creates, classifies, validates, weights, relates, preserves, contradicts, supersedes, and applies evidence during diagnostic reasoning.

core_principle.statement: ARIA shall distinguish what was observed from what was reported, interpreted, inferred, calculated, or concluded. Evidence must preserve provenance and shall influence reasoning according to reliability, directness, applicability, independence, freshness, and technical relevance.
rules: Evidence is not automatically fact.
A source and the information supplied by that source are separate concepts.
Interpretation shall remain traceable to the original artifact or observation.
Repeated representations of the same underlying information shall not become independent corroboration.
Contradictory evidence shall be preserved rather than silently discarded.
Current validated direct evidence may outweigh historical expectation.
ARIA's own inference shall never become independent evidence merely because ARIA generated it.

evidence_types.name: DIRECT_MEASUREMENT
evidence_types.description: A measured technical value obtained directly from equipment, an instrument, telemetry, or another measurement system.

evidence_types.name: SYSTEM_STATE
evidence_types.description: Directly retrieved operational or configuration state from the applicable system.

evidence_types.name: CONFIGURATION_VALUE
evidence_types.description: A specific configured parameter obtained from equipment, management software, configuration export, or other authoritative configuration source.

evidence_types.name: ALARM
evidence_types.description: Alarm, event, or fault indication generated by applicable equipment or management software.

evidence_types.name: LOG_ENTRY
evidence_types.description: Timestamped system or equipment log information.

evidence_types.name: VISUAL_OBSERVATION
evidence_types.description: Condition visible in a photograph, screenshot, video, live view, or direct human observation.

evidence_types.name: USER_REPORT
evidence_types.description: Technical information reported by a human participant.

evidence_types.name: PROCEDURE_RESULT
evidence_types.description: Result produced by executing a defined diagnostic or validation procedure.

evidence_types.name: CHANGE_EVENT
evidence_types.description: Verified change to equipment, configuration, topology, cabling, software, alignment, or another relevant technical state.

evidence_types.name: ENGINEERING_REFERENCE
evidence_types.description: Applicable design, engineering, expected value, link budget, drawing, or baseline reference.

evidence_types.name: DOCUMENTED_TECHNICAL_FACT
evidence_types.description: Technical fact obtained from an applicable authoritative document.

evidence_types.name: HISTORICAL_CASE_EVIDENCE
evidence_types.description: Validated information originating from a previous case and used as contextual experience.

evidence_types.name: DERIVED_EVIDENCE
evidence_types.description: Evidence mathematically or logically derived from one or more underlying evidence records.

evidence_types.name: NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE
evidence_types.description: Validated absence of an expected condition where that absence has diagnostic meaning.

source_types.name: EQUIPMENT_DIRECT
source_types.description: Information retrieved directly from applicable equipment.

source_types.name: NETWORK_MANAGEMENT_SYSTEM
source_types.description: Information retrieved from an applicable NMS, EMS, controller, or management platform.

source_types.name: TEST_INSTRUMENT
source_types.description: Information produced by an applicable test instrument.

source_types.name: CONFIGURATION_EXPORT
source_types.description: Configuration information exported from applicable equipment or management software.

source_types.name: SCREENSHOT
source_types.description: Image capture of a system, measurement, configuration, alarm, or other displayed information.

source_types.name: PHOTO
source_types.description: Photographic evidence of physical equipment, installation, routing, condition, or environment.

source_types.name: VIDEO
source_types.description: Video evidence of physical or operational conditions.

source_types.name: USER
source_types.description: Information provided by a human participant.

source_types.name: ENGINEERING_DOCUMENT
source_types.description: Applicable engineering design or reference documentation.

source_types.name: CUSTOMER_STANDARD
source_types.description: Applicable customer specification, standard, procedure, or acceptance criterion.

source_types.name: ARIA_CALCULATION
source_types.description: A deterministic calculation performed by ARIA from traceable source evidence.

source_types.name: ARIA_INTERPRETATION
source_types.description: An interpretation produced by ARIA from source information. This source type shall not be treated as independent corroborating evidence.

source_types.name: HISTORICAL_CASE
source_types.description: Evidence originating from a previous diagnostic case.

evidence_statuses.name: RECEIVED
evidence_statuses.description: Evidence has been received but has not completed validation.

evidence_statuses.name: VALIDATING
evidence_statuses.description: Evidence is being checked for provenance, interpretation, applicability, reliability, and consistency.

evidence_statuses.name: VALID
evidence_statuses.description: Evidence is sufficiently valid for diagnostic use at its assigned confidence.

evidence_statuses.name: QUESTIONABLE
evidence_statuses.description: Evidence may be useful but contains unresolved reliability, applicability, interpretation, or provenance concerns.

evidence_statuses.name: CONTRADICTED
evidence_statuses.description: Evidence materially conflicts with other credible evidence and the conflict remains unresolved.

evidence_statuses.name: SUPERSEDED
evidence_statuses.description: A newer or more authoritative evidence record represents the applicable technical state.

evidence_statuses.name: INVALID
evidence_statuses.description: Evidence is known to be technically unreliable, incorrectly interpreted, inapplicable, corrupted, or otherwise unsuitable for diagnostic use.

evidence_statuses.name: EXPIRED
evidence_statuses.description: Evidence was valid when obtained but no longer reliably represents the current technical state.

evidence_quality_dimensions.name: SOURCE_RELIABILITY
evidence_quality_dimensions.description: Expected reliability of the originating source for this specific type of information.

evidence_quality_dimensions.name: DIRECTNESS
evidence_quality_dimensions.description: Degree to which the evidence directly observes or measures the condition being evaluated.

evidence_quality_dimensions.name: APPLICABILITY
evidence_quality_dimensions.description: Degree to which the evidence applies to the exact equipment, endpoint, configuration, time, topology, and technical question.

evidence_quality_dimensions.name: FRESHNESS
evidence_quality_dimensions.description: Degree to which the evidence remains representative of the current technical state.

evidence_quality_dimensions.name: INDEPENDENCE
evidence_quality_dimensions.description: Degree to which the evidence provides information independent from other evidence already considered.

evidence_quality_dimensions.name: PROVENANCE_QUALITY
evidence_quality_dimensions.description: Degree to which origin, custody, transformations, and interpretation history are known.

evidence_quality_dimensions.name: EXTRACTION_CONFIDENCE
evidence_quality_dimensions.description: Confidence that information was correctly extracted from its source.

evidence_quality_dimensions.name: MEASUREMENT_QUALITY
evidence_quality_dimensions.description: Quality of the measurement process, instrument, method, calibration state, and operating conditions.

overall_confidence_model.description: Evidence confidence shall combine relevant evidence-quality dimensions without implying that all dimensions are equally important in every context.
rules: Independence shall primarily control corroboration weight rather than whether the evidence itself is true.
A severe weakness in a critical dimension may cap overall evidence confidence.
Exact weighting shall remain configurable and calibratable.
ARIA shall preserve component scores rather than only the combined score.

source_reliability.description: Source reliability is contextual. No source type is universally authoritative for every technical question.
rules: Direct equipment data may be highly reliable for displayed state while still being misleading if the wrong endpoint or interface is being viewed.
A screenshot may strongly establish what was displayed but not necessarily whether the displayed value represents physical reality.
A photograph may strongly establish visible routing but may not establish internal configuration.
A user statement may be highly reliable when the user directly performed and observed the action.
Manufacturer documentation may strongly establish intended product behavior but does not prove the current equipment is behaving accordingly.
Historical experience may influence probability but does not establish the current case condition.

user_report_handling.description: Human statements are legitimate evidence but shall preserve attribution and distinguish observation from interpretation.
rules: ARIA shall preserve what the user actually reported when practical.
A user's technical conclusion shall not automatically become a confirmed fact.
The statement 'I checked the configuration and it is correct' contains both a claimed action and a claimed interpretation.
ARIA may ask for direct supporting evidence when doing so has sufficient diagnostic value.
Validated user-specific history may modify expected report reliability for specific action types, but shall not become a universal credibility score.

artifact_interpretation.description: Information extracted from screenshots, photos, videos, documents, configuration files, and logs shall preserve both the original artifact and the interpreted evidence.
rules: The original artifact shall remain linked to all derived evidence.
Multiple facts extracted from one artifact may exist as separate evidence records while remaining members of the same provenance family.
Extraction confidence shall be recorded when interpretation is uncertain.
ARIA shall distinguish text visibly present in an artifact from conclusions inferred from that text.
If an artifact is unreadable or ambiguous, ARIA shall preserve uncertainty rather than invent values.
Every evidence record shall have traceable origin.
Derived evidence shall identify all underlying evidence records.
Transformations shall not sever linkage to original source material.
Evidence sharing a common underlying source shall be identifiable as dependent.

independence_model.description: ARIA shall distinguish corroboration from repetition.

examples.evidence_a: Technician reports RSL of -58 dBm after reading radio GUI.
examples.evidence_b: Screenshot of the same GUI showing -58 dBm.

examples.evidence_a: Radio GUI reports RSL of -58 dBm.
examples.evidence_b: Independent calibrated field measurement supports the same condition.

rules: Duplicate evidence shall not increase corroboration.
Derived evidence shall not independently corroborate its source.
Partially dependent evidence may add limited confidence but shall not receive full independent weight.
Unknown dependency shall be treated conservatively.

evidence_relationships.name: SUPPORTS
evidence_relationships.description: Evidence increases support for another evidence interpretation, hypothesis, finding, or conclusion.

evidence_relationships.name: CONTRADICTS
evidence_relationships.description: Evidence is materially inconsistent with another evidence record, hypothesis, finding, or conclusion.

evidence_relationships.name: CORROBORATES
evidence_relationships.description: Independent or sufficiently independent evidence supports the same material condition.

evidence_relationships.name: REFINES
evidence_relationships.description: Evidence provides greater specificity without invalidating the broader evidence.

evidence_relationships.name: SUPERSEDES
evidence_relationships.description: Evidence more accurately represents the applicable current state than an older record.

evidence_relationships.name: DERIVED_FROM
evidence_relationships.description: Evidence is calculated or interpreted from another evidence record.

evidence_relationships.name: DUPLICATES
evidence_relationships.description: Evidence represents materially the same underlying information.

evidence_relationships.name: VALIDATES
evidence_relationships.description: Evidence verifies the correctness or expected outcome of an action, measurement, correction, or prior observation.

evidence_relationships.name: INVALIDATES
evidence_relationships.description: Evidence demonstrates that another evidence record or interpretation is unreliable or incorrect.

rules: Contradictory evidence shall not automatically cancel mathematically.
Apparent contradiction may represent a technical state change over time.
Evidence from different endpoints, radios, paths, or interfaces may appear contradictory while both are valid.
ARIA shall attempt to determine whether evidence actually refers to the same technical state before declaring conflict.
Unresolved contradictions shall reduce diagnostic confidence.

temporal_evidence.description: Evidence validity may depend on when it was observed relative to configuration changes, component changes, outages, weather, corrective actions, and other events.
rules: Evidence shall preserve observed time when known.
Evidence obtained before a material state change shall not automatically represent the post-change state.
Older evidence remains historically valid even when superseded for current-state reasoning.
Time-sensitive evidence may expire without being deleted.
Stable technical facts shall not expire solely due to age.

negative_evidence.description: Absence of an expected observation may have diagnostic value only when the observation would reasonably have been expected and detectable.
rules: Failure to observe something is not automatically evidence of absence.
Negative evidence requires an expectation model.
Detection capability must be sufficient.
A missing alarm is weak evidence against a failure when the failure does not reliably generate that alarm.
A clean discriminating test may strongly weaken a hypothesis when the hypothesis predicts a detectable abnormal result.

derived_evidence.description: ARIA may create deterministic derived evidence from validated source evidence.
examples: Difference between engineered and measured RSL
Elapsed time between configuration change and failure onset
rules: Derived evidence shall preserve formulas and source evidence IDs.
Derived evidence confidence shall not exceed what is justified by its source evidence.
A calculation from uncertain inputs remains uncertain.
Derived evidence shall not independently corroborate its own source data.
The same evidence may affect different hypotheses differently.
Evidence may strongly support one hypothesis while being neutral to another.
Evidence may weaken multiple competing hypotheses simultaneously.
ARIA shall record why evidence has a particular diagnostic effect.

evidence_request_policy.description: ARIA shall request additional evidence according to expected diagnostic utility rather than demanding exhaustive information.
rules: Do not request evidence already available and sufficiently reliable.
Request higher-quality evidence when existing evidence uncertainty materially affects diagnosis.
Prefer evidence capable of discriminating between important competing hypotheses.
The burden of obtaining evidence shall be considered by the routing engine.
ARIA may accept lower-confidence evidence temporarily when higher-quality evidence is impractical.
Superseded evidence shall remain in case history.
New evidence shall supersede older evidence only when both represent the same technical property and the newer evidence more appropriately represents the applicable state.
Supersession is not invalidation.
Historical reasoning shall remain reconstructable using the evidence available at the time.
Invalidation requires a recorded reason.
Invalid evidence shall not be deleted.
Probability changes caused by invalid evidence shall be recalculated through a new auditable event.
ARIA shall preserve when and why the evidence was originally believed.

evidence.observation: Technician reports Main RSL -44 dBm and Diversity RSL -63 dBm.
Radio management screenshot displays Main -44.2 dBm and Diversity -63.1 dBm.

example.interpretation: ARIA now has strong evidence that the RSL imbalance exists, but none of these three records independently establishes why it exists.

semantic_rules.rule: Evidence of a symptom is not automatically evidence of its cause.
ARIA shall preserve the distinction between observation, interpretation, inference, and conclusion.
Every material evidence record shall preserve provenance.
Evidence quality shall be evaluated in relation to the technical question it is being used to answer.
Repeated representations of the same underlying information shall not be treated as independent corroboration.
ARIA's interpretation of evidence shall not become an independent source of evidence.
Contradictory evidence shall be preserved and investigated rather than silently discarded.
Evidence may be valid historically while no longer representing the current technical state.
A screenshot establishes what was displayed with greater confidence than it establishes the physical mechanism responsible for the display.
A user report may be diagnostically valuable without being treated as unquestionable fact.
User-specific evidence reliability shall be contextual to evidence and action type rather than represented as a universal personal credibility score.
Direct current evidence may outweigh historical patterns when evidence quality and applicability justify doing so.
Negative evidence has diagnostic value only when the absent condition was reasonably expected and detectable.
Derived evidence shall remain traceable to every source value required to reproduce it.
Invalidation, contradiction, expiration, and supersession are distinct evidence states and shall not be conflated.
Evidence shall not be deleted merely because it was incorrect; its role in prior reasoning shall remain auditable.
When evidence quality cannot be established, ARIA shall represent that uncertainty explicitly.
The language model may extract or interpret evidence but deterministic ARIA services shall control authoritative evidence records and relationships.
ARIA shall seek better evidence when the expected diagnostic benefit justifies the additional burden.
ARIA shall never convert repetition, confidence of tone, or agreement into technical corroboration.
